Passage: Al-Khwarizmi, Father of Algebra

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi was a 9th-century Muslim mathematician and astronomer who worked at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad. His landmark treatise introduced systematic solutions to linear and quadratic equations. The word 'algebra' originates from 'al-jabr', an operation he formalized. Al-Khwarizmi also helped popularize the Hindu-Arabic numeral system, which forms the numerical foundation used worldwide today.
